review.summary: Client-paper MSA for a revenue-management and guest-analytics platform for nine hotels in Saudi Arabia, USD 140,000, 36-month term, KSA law and Riyadh courts, guest data hosted in KSA, 60-day payment. The core problem is that AtliQ's live non-compete with Al Noor Hospitality bars AtliQ and its affiliates from providing data analytics, AI or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC (including Saudi Arabia) until roughly September 2029, and the Gulf Crown waiver letter for Seaside Hotels expressly does not extend to other GCC hospitality clients. Several other clauses (payment days, LD formula, liability carve-outs, foreign governing law, regulated guest data) also need negotiation, but the register conflict is the threshold issue that should go to Karandeep before any commercial terms are discussed.
